body:
Let’s divide this into 2 categories:

**Page load**
Sounds like the scroll position is stored in session storage upon each scroll event. And then applied upon future page loads.

Ideas:
- Don’t store scroll position at all (if possible)
- Clear scroll position in session storage upon page load
- Clear scroll position in session storage upon `onbeforeunload` event

**Route change**
Sounds like default behaviour to have the scroll position preserved

Ideas:
- Set [scrollPositionRestoration](https://angular.io/api/router/ExtraOptions#scrollPositionRestoration) to `enabled`

@dannyskoog 

I think why the scroll position is stored in the first place is because

**Better UX**
When I open the doc in mobile phone, and I put the browser into background by switch app or simply switching the tab because I want to check out something else in another tab opening in the same browser, there are cases when the tab/browser contains the angular doc will be closed because the tab/app we switch to consume too much space in cpu, in a low cpu device, system will make choice for the current running so it will temporarily close the browser/tab that contains the angular doc. 

When this case happens, for a better user experience, for example, when I switch back to browser/tab containing the doc, I must want the previous page I visited remain in the same place, right?

So, I think the better solution will be cleared the session storage when the url is refreshed. Because doc is a single page application, the change it make to the url is not refreshing the address bar, I think.

The fact that you locate where the scroll position is stored is amazing! Good job! And thank you!😄

I see :) Thanks for explaining a use case where one might want to store the scroll position!

Honestly, everything I wrote was just assumptions since I’m on my phone atm :)
The desired outcome is to ***not*** store the scroll position when navigating to a different URL.
Yes, I know @sjtrimble :) And that’s what I gave a few suggestions on how to achieve further up.

> @sjtrimble , what about a feature that we specify while adding routes in the project that:
> 
> {
> path: 'user/:userId', component: UserInfoComponent, preserveScrolls : true
> }
> 
> 1. Whenever we reach a route and this route had a preserveScrolls true, then
>    scroll upto the position that was saved(if any) and on each scroll event update it.
> 2. Whenever we reach a route and this route had a preserveScrolls false.
>    we delete the stored scroll position (if any), and _DO NOT_ update it.

@ishan-srivastava This issue is a documentation issue not relates to the Angular project, the behavior is not caused by Angular router, but [angular.io's own scrolling implementation](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/c529be9f2427d7bd1b0fded23dca58019634f8cd/aio/src/app/shared/scroll.service.ts#L17-L209).
@trotyl , yep that makes sense. They have an explicit logic for that. 👍

issue.body:
Previously, when navigating to a new page via a link, the scroll position was correctly restored to 0, but navigating to a new page via typing the URL in the browser address bar keeps the old scroll position.

This commit ensures that the scroll position is restored to 0 whenever the `ScrollService` is instantiated anew (i.e. new page navigation). The old behavior of retaining the scroll position on reload is kept by storing the old URL when leaving a page and only applying the stored scroll position if the new URL matches the stored one.

Fixes #33260.
